chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who is struck by thirst to the extent that he fears for his life.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He drinks by the measure of what sustains his breath, and he does not drink until he is fully quenched.'
ai.seo_question: How much should a fasting person drink when severely thirsty to avoid breaking the fast completely?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between breaking the fast entirely and merely suspending it due to necessity, emphasizing that one should drink only enough to preserve life (ramaq) rather than satisfying full thirst (ruya). In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the principle of 'la darar' (no harm) while maintaining the fast's validity, provided the person resumes fasting if able, or performs qada later. The ruling highlights the balance between preserving health and fulfilling religious obligation, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, and someone else from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who is hit by thirst to the extent that he fears upon himself.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can drink by a measurement of what he can hold his breath with, and he should not drink to the extent that he his quenched’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Idris and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar who has said the following: “About a man who becomes thirsty and is afraid for his life, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
He can drink to spare his life but not to fill himself up.’”
